articles.title: De la Fuente: "No es lo más adecuado jugar cuatro partidos en diez días"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español antes del partido ante Inglaterra
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español antes del partido ante Inglaterra
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente acaba de comparecer ante los medios de comunicación en la sala de prensa de Wembley para analizar el duelo ante Inglaterra. Mañana, en la catedral del fútbol inglés estrena España su segunda estrella. El contexto: "El mejor escenario para estrenar la segunda estrella. Un rival como Inglaterra... Casi nada. Seguro que el ambiente estará a la altura de un España-Inglaterra". Once: "No, mañana sacaremos a los que creamos que son los adecuados para este partido. Intentaremos acertar con la alineación. Hay jugadores que están mejor o peor que hace dos meses". Riesgo de relajación: "Te garantizo que no habrá relajación. Conozco a estos futbolistas y sé que quieren seguir ganando y quieren seguir haciendo historia. El hambre tiene que ser constante y este equipo lo tiene. Lo que hemos hecho hasta ahora no nos vale. Este equipo tiene un margen de mejora muy grande". El formato y el calendario: "Nadie nos consultó nada. Jugamos cuatro partidos en díez días y me parece una exigencia muy alta. Hay que hacerlo, pero no es lo más adecuado". Peligro de conformismo: "No nos conformamos con lo que hemos hecho. Queremos seguir caminando y haciendo cosas importantes. Jugamos contra la tercera en el ranking FIFA, así que mañana puede pasar de todo. Pero no será por relajación. Lo mejor está por llegar". ¿Le ha cambiado la vida?: "Sí. Después de ganar la Eurocopa el reconocimiento popular fue importante, pero el Mundial es otra dimensión. A nivel mediático, la gente me conoce muchísimo más. No sólo en España, también en otros países. La gente nos ve y viene a darnos las gracias por lo que le hemos hecho vivir. Ver la felicidad en la gente es un orgullo". Inglaterra: "Inglaterra es una gran selección. Han sido finalistas de la Eurocopa, semifinalista del Mundial... Es una potencia. Nosotros intentamos estar siempre a la altura. Se puede ganar y perder, pero nosotros estamos en un momento de confianza y cualquier rival te puede ganar". Once: "Lo tenemos decidido. Sólo puedo decir que estamos muy contentos con los jugadores que tenemos. Siempre hay cambios. Acaba un ciclo, empieza otro... Lamentamos la baja de Marcos Llorente, pero estamos muy contentos con Eric, Porro, Fresneda... Los jugadores que vienen por detrás nos hacen estar muy tranquilos". El control del juego de España: "Imposible de copiar no es. Somos fieles a un modelo asentado en una base sólida. Se evoluciona, se crece. Es el tranbajo de muchos años. Se juega parecido en cada categoría, con los matices de cada generación".

articles.title: ¿Cómo será la nueva camiseta de Atlético Nacional para 2027? El presidente revela detalles inéditos sobre su diseño
articles.standfirst: Atlético Nacional sorprende a sus hinchas: presidente expone los primeros detalles de la camiseta 2027
articles.summary: Atlético Nacional sorprende a sus hinchas: presidente expone los primeros detalles de la camiseta 2027
articles.body: Atlético Nacional se alista para dar un giro histórico en el fútbol colombiano. Luego de anunciar el fin de su alianza de más de 13 años con la multinacional Nike, el conjunto antioqueño confirmó que a partir de 2027 vestiría su propia marca de indumentaria deportiva, convirtiéndose en el primer club del país en asumir de forma directa la confección y distribución de toda su ropa deportiva. El presidente de la institución, Sebastián Arango Botero, aprovechó el marco del evento 'Leyendas' para ofrecer detalles inéditos de este proyecto y explicar la visión detrás de esta ambiciosa apuesta empresarial y deportiva. Durante su intervención, Arango enfatizó el agradecimiento al aliado comercial que los acompañó por más de una década, pero dejó en claro que la institución busca recuperar la autonomía total sobre sus símbolos y productos. "Llegamos aquí después de 14 años de un camino compartido con un gran aliado al cual solo le tenemos gratitud. Y damos este paso porque creemos que el valor de este escudo tiene que volver al club y a su gente", afirmó el directivo. Para el dirigente verdolaga, la camiseta del equipo trascendió el concepto de prenda de vestir para convertirse en un objeto con alto valor emocional e identidad social entre los hinchas. Uno de los anuncios más destacados fue la decisión de confeccionar toda la indumentaria en territorio colombiano, apoyándose en la industria textil nacional. "Porque un club que cree en este país tiene que demostrarlo y hacer país también se juega en la cancha de la industria, del empleo y del desarrollo", ratificó Arango Botero. La iniciativa de la marca propia forma parte de una estrategia integral con la que Atlético Nacional busca consolidarse no solo como una potencia deportiva en la región, sino como una marca con diversas líneas de negocio: Con este movimiento, la institución 'paisa' marca un precedente en la gestión de clubes en Colombia, uniendo identidad, industria nacional y soberanía comercial de cara a la temporada 2027.

articles.body:
Palmer was a controversial omission from England's World Cup squad in the summer, with an injury-hit season impacting his form.

After a summer off, it appeared Palmer was returning to a high level in the early weeks of this campaign, with six goal involvements in seven games for Chelsea. That output earned him a recall to the England group for the Nations League matches with Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia - but Palmer withdrew from the squad due to injury.

It is the second time Palmer has been called up for the national team and then withdrawn with a fitness problem since Tuchel took charge of England at the start of 2025. Palmer has also missed three England camps entirely with injury and wasn't selected for another.

Put to him that Palmer doesn't seem desperate to play for England, Tuchel responded: "It's hard to argue against what you're saying."

Asked where that leaves England, Tuchel replied: "It leaves us with Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze.

"All in camp, all desperate to be here, all available and all ready to go. Ready to stop a holiday after one day in Dubai [as was the case with Gibbs-White] and fly back."

Tuchel added: "I can only judge him on what he [Palmer] is delivering for the national team and he's just missing too many opportunities.

"If Declan [Rice] calls me, and he explains to me, and I see against Brighton straight away that something is off that confirmed that impression, every case is different.

"I know from Marcus [Rashford] and Kobbie [Mainoo] that they play with discomfort for their clubs. I know it looks strange if Kobbie and Marcus finish a game at the weekend for their clubs and then suddenly are not here, but okay - first of all, in doubt, we trust the players.

"I have no reason not to trust the players because they were with us in the US and they were fantastic. Tino Livramento also pulled out. This is normal.

"I just refuse to put too much into it. I refuse to believe it."

Palmer has played three times for Tuchel, across two camps, and the England boss had said earlier that his lack of availability is a problem.

"For sure it's a missed opportunity," Tuchel said.

"It's another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities.

"I don't blame him for it, it's just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries.

"I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity."

Palmer played the full 90 minutes for Chelsea at Brentford on the Friday before the international break began. Asked what the specific injury issue is for Palmer, Tuchel rejected the suggestion this was a case of the forward's workload being managed.

"He plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain," said Tuchel. "Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We're not managing load.

"This is not an 'international break'. It's a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That's what we created. We will never compromise on that.

"We will never let this feeling creep in that the players don't want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England."

Analysis: Is Tuchel losing patience with Palmer?

"It sounds like Thomas Tuchel is almost losing patience with Cole Palmer because for the past two years since Tuchel has been the England manager, Palmer has hardly ever featured for England, he always seems to be injured.

"But Palmer has started every game apart from one for Chelsea this season - and I'd put money on the fact he'll be playing for Chelsea as soon as the international break is over.

"Tuchel basically said, 'if you're not here, you can't impress me' and it opens the door for someone else to impress the England manager.

"If you still want to impress Tuchel, you can still join up and take part in the England camp. There have been instances in the past, like Jude Bellingham - when he was going through a rocky spell in his relationship with Tuchel and he was injured - he still went joined up on international duty and that impressed Tuchel.

"So you have to ask why Palmer is not involved with England at all for the whole three weeks. Is his injury really that bad that it stops him playing or training, or showing his face at all?

"Palmer is also fighting to be the England No 10. England have also got Bellingham and Morgan Rogers so in Tuchel's mind, he doesn't feel that he needs Palmer that much because he has other options.

"Morgan Gibbs-White as well, who is going to have the opportunity to impress him over the next couple of weeks."

Kane: Everyone proud to play for England

Palmer is one of five players to have withdrawn from the original squad named by Tuchel, with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento also making way.

England captain Harry Kane was asked about those withdrawals and whether he was concerned players weren't prioritising playing for their country enough at this stage of the season and international cycle after the World Cup.

"Everyone is extremely proud to be an England player," he said.

"Everyone has their own individual circumstances, physical situations, mental situations. That's down to the player and coach to talk and sort out.

"It's going to be a bit of a gruelling schedule [playing four games in 11 days] but I look forward to those things.

"Ultimately it's about what you do on the training pitch - and from the start of this week it's been at the highest level."

articles.title: Mbappé marca el primer gol de la era Zidane y se lesiona: "No pinta bien"
articles.standfirst: Sufre una lesión tendinosa y está descartado para el resto de la concentración
articles.summary: Sufre una lesión tendinosa y está descartado para el resto de la concentración
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé ha encendido todas las alarmas en Francia... y el sonido llega hasta el Real Madrid. Después de que Konaté abandonase la concentración, el ariete galo se dolió de la rodilla en el encuentro contra Turquía y deberá dejar el equipo francés, como anunció la Federación: "Sufre una lesión tendinosa y está descartado para el resto de la concentración". La acción tuvo lugar antes de llegar a la hora de partido. Justo, de hecho, en el momento de conectar el remate con el que abrió el marcador y, por ende, estrenó la era Zinédine Zidane a los mandos de la selección francesa. Recibió en el 'piquito' izquierdo del área, cargó la pierna... y, en el momento de ir a celebrar, notó que algo no estaba bien. La dolencia, concretamente, se produjo en la pierna izquierda. Es decir, la del apoyo en el momento de golpear el balón. De hecho, justo en el momento que conecta con el esférico, Mbappé pega un pequeño salto, a modo de acto reflejo, y, en el momento que echa a correr para celebrar, se detuvo de inmediato. Rápidamente, los médicos de 'les bleus' saltaron al césped para realizarle una primera exploración. Kylian trató de seguir jugando. Pero, nada más regresar al césped y probarse con una primera carrera, se volvió a tirar al suelo pidiendo el cambio. Los gestos de dolor, tapándose la cara incluso, reflejaban cierta preocupación. Fue Désiré Doué quien entró en su lugar. Ya en rueda de prensa, Zidane ofreció una primera versión... y no fue nada alentadora: "No pinta bien, por desgracia. Creo que tendrá que volver. No vamos a correr ningún riesgo. Desarrolló hiperextensión en la rodilla durante el chut. No es muy alentador que pueda continuar". La federación francesa, por su parte, informó que "abandonará la concentración de la selección francesa antes de los últimos tres partidos". Mbappé, recordemos, ya se vio obligado a parar la temporada pasada por unos problemas en esta misma rodilla izquierda. Lo hizo, de hecho, hasta en dos ocasiones... después de que se destapase que el primer examen no se le realizó en la rodilla que tenía afectada por parte de los servicios médicos.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Premier League club found guilty of breaking majority of 115 financial rules
articles.summary: Manchester City have been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching.
articles.body:
Manchester City have been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching.

The Athletic , external is reporting that the sanctions have not been decided but that the independent panel has reached its decision, finding the club guilty of all but one count.

Asked if the report was correct, City did not comment either way.

Instead they released a statement saying the "Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality".

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence," it added.

BBC Sport has also been told that, in the event of being found guilty, City will appeal against the findings.

Other Premier League clubs are believed to have been informed about the independent panel's decision and have sought legal advice as to whether they would have a compensation claim.

Clubs seek legal advice over Man City charges compensation

Relegation? Titles stripped? Appeals? What next for Man City

In February 2023, City were charged with more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules following a four-year investigation.

The club was referred to an independent commission over allegations it breached financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

The hearing began in September 2024 behind closed doors and concluded that December after around 12 weeks.

The Premier League claimed City breached rules requiring the club to provide "accurate financial information that gives a true and fair view of the club's financial position".

City strongly denied all charges and have said their case is supported by a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence".

The club won eight trophies in the period covered by the case, including three Premier League titles, three League Cups, one Community Shield and one FA Cup.

The charges cover the mangerial tenures of Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini, and the first two years under Pep Guardiola, who left the club after 10 seasons at the end of the 2025-26 campaign.

A separate case between City and the Premier League was also heard last year.

In 2024, an independent arbitration panel found against aspects of the league's Associated Party Transaction regulations (APTs) after City launched an arbitration challenge.

A tribunal held in February 2025 found the Premier League's rules governing sponsorship deals from the period between 2021 and 2024 are "void and unenforceable".

City and the Premier League reached a settlement in September 2025, with the club accepting the APT rules are valid and binding and both parties agreeing to terminate legal proceedings.

The rules were formed by the Premier League to prevent clubs from profiting from commercial deals with companies linked to their owners that are deemed above "fair market value".

• 54x Failure to provide accurate financial information 2009-10 to 2017-18.

• 14x Failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

• 5x Failure to comply with Uefa's rules including Financial Fair Play (FFP) 2013-14 to 2017-18.

• 7x Breaching Premier League's Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR) 2015-16 to 2017-18.

• 35x Failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations December 2018 - Feb 2023.

There have been suggestions by the Times and football finance expert Kieran Maguire the number of charges is as high as 130. BBC Sport has been unable to verify this.

articles.title: Calidad y efectividad, ¡divino tesoro! El Girona vence a un Alba que perdona lo indecible
articles.standfirst: Abel Ruiz y Van de Beek, que volvió a marcar dos años después, sentencian a un equipo que las tuvo de todos los colores ante un gran Gazzaniga
articles.summary: Abel Ruiz y Van de Beek, que volvió a marcar dos años después, sentencian a un equipo que las tuvo de todos los colores ante un gran Gazzaniga
articles.body: La calidad y la efectividad fueron factores claves para explicar la victoria del Girona ante un Albacete que queda todavía más tocado por el cómo perdió. En el primer acto los tantos de Abel Ruiz y Van de Beek escondieron un dominio claro de los visitantes, que después del 1-0 tuvieron numerosas ocasiones de gol. En el segundo, Gazzaniga, la falta de acierto y la madera acabaron por desesperar a un Alba que sigue sin vencer, en el pozo de la tabla y que acabó con un diez al ser expulsado Sergio Ortuño al final. El Girona, en cambio, se instala en la zona alta con su cuarta victoria en las últimas cinco jornadas y pone presión a sus rivales directos, aunque jugando así, en el próximo duelo ante el Mallorca lo tendrá mucho más complicado El partido comenzó bien para los intereses del Girona, que después de ver cómo el Albacete salía valiente y presionando arriba asestó un golpe a los manchegos en la primera llegada que tuvo. El peligro lo inició Álex Moreno, que desde la banda izquierda puso un centro pasado al segundo palo donde llegó Boñar para descolgar el balón y ceder casi a placer a un Abel Ruiz con la pierna a punto para batir a Carlos Marín. El conjunto visitante no se inmutó al gol blanquirrojo, pasó a ser claro dominador del encuentro, lo que le permitió tener ocasiones, y mereció mucho más. Avisó a través de varias acciones de Álex Rubio y Víctor Valverde, desafortunados o empequeñecidos ante un buen Gazzaniga, o un disparo de Corpas después de un rechace corto. A los catalanes se les hizo una bola el encuentro pese a que en el tramo final del primer acto estiraron líneas con unos buenos Sarasa, Carles Pérez y Abel Ruiz, todo lo activos que podían. Y así desde la banda derecha de Carles Pérez llegó el 2-0 después que el extremo dejara atrás a Agus Medina y cediera a Van de Beek, que controló orientado, se giró y marcó con un potente zurdazo que golpeó en el larguero antes de entrar. La segunda parte comenzó con otras dos grandes ocasiones visitantes, pero el derechazo de Soberón lo sacó con una gran mano Gazzaniga, al igual que el posterior remate de Corpas cara a cara con el meta, que volvió a resultar providencial. Pese a que las llegadas de los de Alberto González seguían siendo regulares, el Girona volvió a dar un paso al frente de la mano de un buen Van de Beek y alguna ocasión de Carles Pérez, pero Neva sacó bajo palos el buen remate de Carles Pérez y Boñar tampoco acertó por poco. Los visitantes acabaron desquiciados y a Álex Rubio se le anuló un gol por fuera de juego, Sergio Ortuño remató a la madera antes de ser expulsado en el minuto 91 y al final Higinio cabeceó demasiado cruzado con todo a favor en el área pequeña un centro de Álex Rubio. El de Beniel volvió a jugar un partido oficial una vez superada la lesión en el cruzado anterior de la rodilla izquierda. Portu fue ovacionado por su afición y estuvo cerca del gol a pase de Boñar. Quien sí marcó fue Van de Beek, que no lo hacía desde el 14 de diciembre del 2024 ante el Mallorca, próximo rival gironí, en Montilivi.

articles.title: Man City charges: Fans react to club being found guilty of majority of financial rule breaches
articles.summary: How Manchester City fans have reacted to news that the club have been found guilty of a majority of the financial rule breaches they were accused of.
articles.body:
The verdict appears to be in - Manchester City have been found guilty of the majority of the 115 financial rule breaches they were charged with.

Following the initial charges brought forward in February 2023, relating to the Premier League's financial rules, a decision was seemingly delivered on Friday in a moment that sent shockwaves around English football.

City, though, have always denied wrongdoing and BBC Sport has been told they would appeal were they found guilty.

But, long before the arrival of the Abu Dhabi ownership group, Pep Guardiola, Premier League title triumphs and the holy grail of the Champions League, City supporters - like any other side - have been the fabric of the football club.

Managers and players come and go but fans remain through thick and thin - now they must face up to possible sanctions which could include a points deduction, financial penalties or even removal from the Premier League.

Three years ago, City were charged and referred to an independent commission over alleged breaches that were said to have taken place between 2009 and 2018.

During that period, the club won three Premier League titles - including their first in 2011-12 - one FA Cup and three EFL Cups.

Man City fan David Mooney, from the Blue Moon podcast, told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I am a bit shocked and stunned about how to process it.

"I imagine as time goes on it will just come with a tinge of disappointment, more than anything else. It is a really weird feeling to process. It has been such a good time over this last 10 years or so, it questions your own experience.

"On the one hand you've got this great enjoyment from the team you have supported all your life winning unprecedented success and playing football like we've never seen before.

"But then having in the back of your mind that everybody thinks we have cheated to do this and everybody thinks this is illegitimate, and that it hasn't been fairly achieved.

"If Manchester City are guilty then the City fans are just as much the victims in this as everybody else because their feelings have been used as well.

"It's just that they had a good time for 10 years and now have to face reality."

The current generation of City fans only know about success, but those from yesteryear know all about watching their side playing in the old Division Two.

Their promotion via the play-offs at the end of the 1998-99 season came after facing the likes of York City, Oldham Athletic and Chesterfield in the league.

Fast forward almost three decades, City now possess one of the best strikers in the world in Erling Haaland, who reached 100 Premier League goals faster than anyone in the competition's history.

City sit top of the table after winning all five of their league games so far and their first game after the international break is a trip to face Liverpool at Anfield.

City fan Matt said on 5 Live: "I think I need therapy now. It has escalated over the last few hours. It's so hard to be a die-hard Blue. The decision is made, yet we haven't appealed it or really made a statement yet.

"I was there when Paul Dickov scored back in Division Two. We celebrated that success and went on to do incredible things. We have a song about going down with a billion in the bank.

"If we get titles taken off us, point deductions, we come out of this league, then we will fight until the end. I can't wait to see Erling Haaland bag a hat-trick against Grimsby.

"You go through the good times and the hard times. We have to go to Liverpool and it's going to be very interesting to see how we react. We boo the Champions League anthem, well what about the Premier League?"

Champions League win 'will never be taken away from me'

After missing out to Chelsea in the 2021 Champions League final, City finally claimed the biggest prize in European club football two years later by beating Inter Milan.

For many, it was an 'I was there' moment.

Season ticket holder John said on 5 Live: "I was in Istanbul [for the 2023 Champions League final], that will never be taken away from me what I experienced that day, the build-up to the game and the game, and the day after, and everything that went along with it.

"That will never be taken away from me, regardless of what's been decided in the court or elsewhere along with the Premier League."

Fellow supporter David Wilson told BBC News: "You will never take away all the memories of all those moments and trophies from City fans. Those will live on regardless what happens over the next weeks, months and years.

"There are many fans who were there when we were in the lower divisions, and they will stick by the club. What we want as fans is an explanation as to why - if we have been found guilty - we have dragged it out so long. Some context behind it.

"True City fans, and fans who have been there all their lives, will still love the club dearly no matter what other people say."

articles.title: USMNT's Pochettino Addresses World Cup Controversy, Says 'Energy Changed' After Balogun Ruling
articles.summary: USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino says he regrets not getting "more involved" in the decision to suspend a red card for striker Folarin Balogun he says changed the energy of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
articles.body:
USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino says he regrets not getting "more involved" in the decision to suspend a red card for striker Folarin Balogun he says changed the energy of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Pochettino addressed Balogun's red card, which was suspended by FIFA after a reported discussion between federation president Gianni Infantino and U.S. president Donald Trump, in a Spanish language interview with Andrés Cantor published Friday by Fútbol de Primera.

"That loss against Belgium was the consequence of certain things... I should have been much more involved, or should have been part of that decision-making process," Pochettino said about the red card suspension (translation h/t The Athletic's Paul Tenorio ).

Pochettino initially supported FIFA's decision to walk back the red card, arguing the United States had already paid by playing without Balogun for almost half of a Round of 32 matchup against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

The decision marked what appeared to be the first time in 64 years a player received a World Cup red card without also serving a suspension, per the Associated Press.

Pochettino said at the time he was "not involved" in the push to lift Balogun's suspension but that U.S. Soccer had been "working on trying to defend our situation," per ESPN's Jeff Carlisle .

The USMNT was then eliminated from the Round of 16 after conceding a 4-1 loss to Belgium in Seattle.

"At the time, I didn't fully understand the criticism and everything else," Pochettino said in his recent interview with Cantor, per Tenorio. "But now, with the benefit of time and looking back on it, the truth is that you have to learn from things, from mistakes. And I think sometimes the things that happen during a tournament have to stay there."

Pochettino continued, per Tenorio: "You have to have the humility to recognize that sometimes you can be wrong. And I think my mistake was not being present at that moment.

"Things happened, and the truth is that the entire energy changed. And that game is very difficult to analyze because it took place in an environment that was not the best environment in which to go and compete at a World Cup."

Pochettino signed an extension with U.S. Soccer last month that brought his tenure as USMNT's head coach through 2030, including the 2030 FIFA World Cup in Morocco, Portugal and Spain.

For now, Pochettino will turn his attention to his program's first action since their July 6 loss to Belgium. A USMNT roster not featuring Balogun, Christian Pulisic or Weston McKennie will get what Pochettino described as a "fresh start" when beginning an upcoming international break Saturday with a friendly against Peru.

articles.title: La nueva Italia de Mancini sigue igual y pierde en su 'redebut'
articles.standfirst: Una gran primera parte de Bélgica desnuda todas las carencias de los transalpinos en su regreso a la competición oficial donde sólo Donnaruma evitó un bochorno mayor
articles.summary: Una gran primera parte de Bélgica desnuda todas las carencias de los transalpinos en su regreso a la competición oficial donde sólo Donnaruma evitó un bochorno mayor
articles.body: Comentaba Mancini en la previa del partido que "se siente en deuda y quiere recuperar a quienes se sienten traicionados", pero la realidad es que con este primer partido le va a costar convencer a los dudosos. Arrancaba Italia un nuevo ciclo con la ilusión de poder dar con la tecla de manera definitiva, con quién mejor que con el último técnico que les llevó a levantar un título; la Eurocopa 2021, pero nada más lejos de la realidad. Bélgica empezó el partido teniendo el balón, pareciendo testear por dónde iría esta nueva Italia. Pero enseguida el nuevo proyecto de Mark van Bommel se desmelenó y comenzó a arrollar a los locales en el Olímpico de Roma, apoyado en la figura estelar de Mika Godts. El extremo izquierdo, ausente en el Mundial, demostró su valía para fichar este pasado verano por el equipo de Luis Enrique, comandando todos los ataques vertiginosos de los belgas. Ayudado por la calamitosa defensa italiana, muy alejada de lo que en algún momento fue, consiguió batir a Donnaruma tras una gran jugada en la que sentó a dos zagueros y derribar el muro transalpino en la segunda clara ocasión, después de ganarle el duelo unos minutos antes a De Ketelaere en un mano a mano. A raíz del gol, sólo una exhibición bajo palos del portero del Manchester City evitó un bochorno mayor. Bélgica perdonó muchas ocasiones ante Donnaruma, con cuatro paradas en apenas media hora, y se fue al descanso con una renta mínima, con las dudas de si se iba a tener que acordar de no haberlo cerrado para la segunda parte. A la vuelta de vestuarios, la Selección italiana mostró otra cara muy diferente. Lammens, que fue espectador de lujo en la primera mitad, tuvo que emplearse a fondo a los disparos de Kean y Esposito a bocajarro. Una falta de eficacia en los tiros de ambos delanteros que seguramente expliquen los resultados de los últimos años para la 'Azzurra'. Sin embargo, y cuando mejor estaban los locales, llegó el martillo por parte de Lukébakio. El exjugador del Sevilla entró de suplente y sólo tardó 10 minutos en silenciar el estadio romanista. Condujo un contraataque por la banda derecha, y recortó hacia dentro para disparar con la zurda al palo largo y hacer imposible la estirada de Donnaruma. Desde entonces, Italia entró en colapso y apenas volvió a inquietar la meta visitante. Un larguero de Scalvini casi bajo palos fue lo más peligroso en un equipo que demostró tener muchas carencias; también en un centro del campo que se intuye de élite con Tonali y Barella, que recibió una tremenda pitada a su salida del campo. El nuevo proyecto de van Bommel arranca con buen pie con las nuevas promesas en el frente del ataque. La Italia de Mancini, por su parte, sigue sumida en las dudas tras dejar una imagen muy pobre en su regreso a la competición oficial.

articles.standfirst: Un doblete del dominicano dio el cuarto triunfo consecutivo de los blanquillos
articles.summary: Un doblete del dominicano dio el cuarto triunfo consecutivo de los blanquillos
articles.body: Óscar Ureña fue el factor decisivo en el duelo entre el Ibiza y el Real Zaragoza. El extremo saltó en la segunda mitad para anotar un doblete y darle a los maños la cuarta victoria consecutiva. Los ibicencos pierden su primer partido en casa. Nada más comenzar los locales estuvieron cerca de adelantarse pero Westerveld envió a córner. Los aragoneses respondieron con Vadillo y Terrer que rozaron el primero de la noche. Prieto también estuvo muy seguro. Ambos tuvieron llegadas peligrosas pero fallaron en la decisión final y se llegó al descanso sin goles. Tras el descanso, Ibai introdujo en el campo a Ureña. Ese cambió fue clave. Y es que, en el primer cuarto de hora de la segunda mitad, el dominicano resolvió el partido. Primero recogió un balón que le llegó de rebote de Espiau y batió a Prieto con un tiro cruzado. Apenas tres minutos después, el propio Espiau falló un mano a mano y el balón volvió a caerle a Ureña que, sin portero, no perdonó. En el tramo final, el Ibiza vio como le anulaban un gol por fuera de juego y Eslava estuvo a centímetros de acortar distancias. Espiau tuvo tiempo para errar otro duelo con Prieto. Los zaragocistas resistieron para ascender a la segunda posición, solo por detrás del filial Villarreal. articles.title: Tim Tebow Pauses Relationship with Christian Organization Accused of Using Predatory Sales Tactics
articles.summary: GAINESVILLE, Fla. (AP) — Tim Tebow said Friday he is "pausing his relationship" with Life Surge, a Christian organization that's been accused of using predatory sales tactics to exploit its followers' faith and financial insecurity.
articles.body:
GAINESVILLE, Fla. (AP) — Tim Tebow said Friday he is "pausing his relationship" with Life Surge, a Christian organization that's been accused of using predatory sales tactics to exploit its followers' faith and financial insecurity.

Tebow, the 2007 Heisman Trophy winner who is currently a college football analyst with ESPN's SEC Nation, said his team is conducting an internal investigation. He spoke on campus in advance of the Mississippi-Florida game at Florida Field on Saturday.

"The allegations are extremely, extremely serious, and it's something that we take very serious," Tebow said. "So, for us, we're having our team do an investigation, but also pausing our relationship 'til we can learn more about the facts to be able to understand more."

Tebow said he was "caught off guard" by the "Pablo Torre Finds Out" podcast that focused partly on Tebow's speaking engagements with Life Surge.

"I was at an anti-human trafficking conference (Thursday), and my team shared (it) with me when we were leaving as we were flying to Alabama for the event, and kind of caught off guard with some of it," Tebow said. "I think that's why I'm really trying to understand more of the facts to really learn it."

His message to his loyal followers amid the allegations:

"It's really important to get answers to understand every bit of that," he said. "My heart ... was to be able to share something that I love to share, which is the love of Christ and the good news of the gospel. And so I think it's really important that we can really understand all the facts and details of it."

The podcast's investigation raised questions about Tebow's knowledge of the organization's practices.

Life Surge, which hosts around 30 events annually, typically brings in Christian celebrities like Tebow to headline events. At Life Surge's one-day events, attendees are urged to sign up for impact classes that pitch packages ranging from $10,000 to $40,000, according to the podcast.

If attendees can't afford the price tag, Life Surge reportedly connects them with third-party lenders who encourage them to apply for credit cards or take out home-equity loans, according to the podcast.

Life Surge has denied any wrongdoing, according to the podcast.

articles.title: UK Prime Minister says football fans 'singled out' by alcohol ban not imposed on rugby matches
articles.summary: Andy Burnham called the alcohol ban at men's football stadiums "discrimination," suggesting a trial could be explored for fans in the stands.
articles.body: United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham is pushing back against England’s restrictions on alcohol at men’s soccer matches, calling the ban "discrimination" and suggesting the rules could be tested on a trial basis. Burnham told reporters, "I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out," as he argued that they should not face restrictions that do not apply to spectators at other sporting events. Under current laws, fans are prohibited from drinking alcohol in view of the pitch at stadiums hosting clubs in England’s top five tiers of men’s football. Those restrictions do not apply to other sports. ANDY BURNHAM TAKES OVER AS UK PRIME MINISTER, CALLS FOR 'NEW POLITICAL MODEL' The Football Supporters’ Association, which advocates for football fans in England and Wales, has called for the "outdated" legislation to be reviewed. Police chiefs, however, have warned against relaxing the law and want to meet with Burnham to "explain the challenges." The legislation dates to 1985, when it was introduced by Margaret Thatcher’s government for football grounds in England and Wales. Then-Home Secretary Leon Brittan said alcohol was a "major contributory factor in violent and disorderly behavior" at stadiums. Burnham’s connection to the sport is personal. He is a proud football fan and a season-ticket holder at Everton, the Premier League club. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Prior to becoming the head of government of the U.K., Burnham spoke out against restrictions on football fans while attending a rugby league match at Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium. Unlike during men’s football games, spectators were allowed to consume alcohol in the stands. While in New York City for the United Nations General Assembly, Burnham was asked whether his position had changed now that he was in Downing Street. "I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different," the prime minister replied. "And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done. It could happen on a trial basis. But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently." Government sources told the BBC that Burnham was restating a long-held personal view rather than announcing a new government policy. Within government, however, the comments are not being interpreted as a sign that Burnham intends to change the law, according to the outlet. A spokesman for the U.K. Football Policing Unit warned that changing the law could create new challenges for police and raise concerns about the "safety of staff and fans at football games." The spokesman said: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behavior from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behavior." FSA chairman Tom Greatrex pushed back against that argument, saying it was "unfair to criminalize football fans for having a pint while watching the match, especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol (while) watching an Oasis gig or rugby league." articles.title: Mbappe goal overshadowed by knee injury to mar Zidane debut France win
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe scores the only goal of France’s win in Turkiye, but Real Madrid striker immediately forced off by injury.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe scored the only goal of the game before having to come off grimacing with a knee injury, as France won 1-0 in Turkiye in the UEFA Nations League in new coach Zinedine Zidane’s first game in charge on Friday.

The Real Madrid star was moved out to the left wing by his new coach after being used through the middle of the France attack under former coach Didier Deschamps at the recent World Cup, which he ended as the top scorer with 10 goals.

It was from the left that Mbappe, France’s all-time top scorer, notched his 67th international goal, controlling and firing into the net low at the near post after being set up by Michael Olise.

He winced in pain as his teammates came across to celebrate the goal at the Kocaeli Stadium in Izmit, about 100km outside Istanbul.

Mbappe tried to carry on after receiving treatment, but eventually slumped to the ground and looked concerned as he prodded the outside of his left knee, before walking off to be replaced by Desire Doue.

France and Real will now nervously wait to discover the extent of the injury, with Les Bleus playing three more games over the next 10 days before the club season resumes.

The sight of his star player and skipper coming off overshadowed Zidane’s first match since being appointed coach in late July on a deal to 2030.

The France legend and 1998 World Cup winner is making his return to elite coaching for the first time since his second stint in charge of Madrid ended in 2021.

France, beaten in the semifinals at the World Cup by eventual winners Spain, are in Group A1 of this edition of the Nations League and will now go to Brussels to face Belgium on Monday. Belgium won 2-0 away to Italy on Friday.

Zidane, whose last match as a player came for France against Italy in the 2006 World Cup final, will then make his home debut as coach against the Italians at the Stade de France next Friday.

His first team selection was not dramatically different from the side that regularly played at the World Cup, although Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert was in at left-back while Manchester City’s Rayan Cherki came into the starting XI.

Olise, the Bayern Munich star who lit up the World Cup, was unlucky not to open the scoring late in the first half when his superb strike was tipped over by home goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir.

France goalkeeper Mike Maignan responded at the start of the second half as he tipped over an attempt by Abdulkerim Bardakci for Turkiye, who finished bottom of their group at the World Cup, despite a 3-2 win over cohosts the United States.

Mbappe’s goal came shortly after, and the visitors later saw Jules Kounde hit the post before Turkiye were reduced to 10 men late on.

Cakir came flying out of his area to halt Bradley Barcola as the France substitute raced through on goal. German referee Felix Zwayer initially waved play on before undertaking a VAR review, after which he decided the goalkeeper had handled the ball, which meant a red card.

Turkiye, coached by former Italian international Vincenzo Montella, will host Italy next on Monday.

articles.title: England U21 4-2 Kazakhstan U21: Will Lankshear scores on debut to wrap up entertaining qualifying win for Young Lions
articles.summary: Match report as Josh Acheampong and Max Alleyne strike, before Will Lankshear rounds off the scoring with a debut goal as England U21s move another step closer to qualifying for next year's European U21 Championship with a 4-2 win against Kazakhstan
articles.body:
Slovakia's defeat to the Republic of Ireland earlier meant England's win put them six points clear with two games left, with a hugely superior goal difference and on the brink of qualification for the tournament in Albania and Serbia.

Kazakhstan sit at the bottom of Group D and their last win in the competition came in June 2025, so it was a big shock when they took the lead over the group leaders in the third minute courtesy of Artyom Litosh's close-range strike.

England soon showed their quality, though they required some luck when Ali Turganov's own goal got them level before Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong produced a striker's finish to put them in front.

Kazakhstan again stunned Molineux to get level through Saif Popov before the break but England managed to secure the win through Max Alleyne's second-half strike before Will Lankshear's debut goal wrapped up the points.

Many expected England to make a quick start but it was the minnows who put themselves in front when Miras Omatay's corner landed at the feet of Litosh who was left unmarked six yards out to poke home in the third minute.

The Young Lions were level after Kazakhstan tried to get rid of a ball into the box, but a clearance from Sultan Askarov ricocheted off the back of Turganov to get them level.

Lee Carsley's side were in front six minutes later when Chelsea youngster Acheampong lined one up from range and fired into the bottom left corner with a pinpoint strike.

The game developed into shooting practice for England, however, against the run of play, Kazakhstan came biting back again and after Popov saw his first effort saved by James Beadle, it bounced back in his favour to turn home the rebound.

A neatly worked free-kick routine got England's noses back in front as Ethan Nwaneri's floated free-kick was nodded back across by Acheampong who turned provider for fellow centre-back Alleyne to sweep home.

Beadle was called into action again to stop Kazakhstan from equalising at the end before Lankshear went down the other end and poked home from Jobe Bellingham's cross to seal the win.

articles.title: Man City Premier League charges: What does the appeals process look like and what happens now?
articles.summary: Man City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 alleged breaches of the league's financial rules back in February 2023; the hearing led by independent commission concluded in December 2024; Inquiry moves to appeal stage amid reports majority of charges 'proven'
articles.body:
If any of the breaches are proven, it is highly likely Manchester City will appeal. In this case, both sides can appeal within 14 days of the judgment.

Any appeal would be heard by a new three-person commission.

A judgement can be appealed on grounds such as fraud, misconduct, or gross unfairness by the arbitrator. City cannot appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

In 2014, City chairman Khaldoon al-Mubarak said he would rather spend £30m on the best 50 lawyers in the world and sue UEFA for the next 10 years than agree a financial penalty for alleged Financial Fair Play breaches.

Premier League rules on appeals and role of the Appeal Board

A party to the proceedings that wishes to challenge a decision of the Commission may do so under Section W of the Premier League Rules.

An Appeal Board is appointed by the chair of the independent judicial panel, Sir Gary Hickinbottom, and must have three members, one of whom should have held judicial office, and would sit as the chair of the Appeal Board.

The proceedings of the Appeal Board are confidential and heard in private.

The Appeal Board has wide discretion in respect of the appeal, and may allow it, dismiss it, or make any order that it deems fit (including varying the order of Commission).

There are a range of sanctions available to the independent commission which include fines, points deductions and other sporting sanctions.

The Premier League do not have set sanctions for financial rule breaches. Clubs decided not to have them because there were fears clubs would break the rules and just take the punishment if they knew what the punishment was going to be.

In February 2025, Richard Masters said the Premier League were looking at having a Sanctions Grid - setting out agreed sanctions for different rules breaches.

Everton were deducted six points on appeal during the 2023/24 season and then two points for profit and sustainability rules (PSR) breaches. Nottingham Forest were deducted four points in the same season.

In the 2008/09 season, Luton Town were deducted 30 points (10 points for illegal payments to agents and 20 points for exiting administration without a Company Voluntary Arrangement (CVA).

In 2021/22 seson, Derby County were deducted 21 points (12 points for entering administration and nine points for financial irregularities).

Can sanctions be imposed while an appeal is under way?

There would be a separate hearing to determine sanctions.

Would the appeal be the end of the matter?

The appeal would be the end of this part of the process. No appeal to CAS would be possible.

There would likely to be more legal cases though, with clubs potentially taking action against City over missing out on trophies and Champions League qualification.

articles.title: Verona, antes del Mundial: "El ciclismo son ciclos; ahora parece que estamos entrando en uno mejor"
articles.standfirst: Carlos Verona habla con MARCA antes del Mundial, con Juan Ayuso y Enric Mas como bazas españolas y una selección cargada de ilusión
articles.summary: Carlos Verona habla con MARCA antes del Mundial, con Juan Ayuso y Enric Mas como bazas españolas y una selección cargada de ilusión
articles.body: Carlos Verona llega al Mundial con ese aire sereno de quien conoce el oficio y las esperas. Habla de piernas, de jerarquías naturales y de una selección española que vuelve a mirar hacia arriba. A unas horas de la carrera, todo parece reducido a lo esencial: estar, saber sufrir y elegir bien el momento. Pregunta. Es viernes por la tarde, ¿cómo ve a España a unas horas de la gran cita mundialista? Respuesta. Yo creo que bien. Juan y yo acabamos de llegar hace unas horas, así que no sé cómo está el resto, pero al final es un Mundial especial. Enric viene de ganar LaVuelta, así que la motivación es alta. Y Juan también ha hecho las cosas muy bien, ha preparado este Mundial a conciencia. Ahora ya estamos en la cuenta atrás, que siempre es la que se hace un poquito más larga. P. La pregunta que se hace mucha gente en España es cómo está Juan. Usted lo sabe bien porque ha estado con él todos estos días. R. Yo creo que bien. Al final se recuperó un poco de ese infortunio que tuvo en Quebec y que luego arrastró en Montreal. Hemos estado entrenando bastante bien, estuvimos en Vermont diez días. La verdad es que es un sitio muy chulo para entrenar, con buenas carreteras. Hemos podido trabajar bastante bien. Entrenar siempre es diferente a competir, pero yo creo que el trabajo está hecho. Ahora toca demostrarlo en la carretera y ver si realmente todo va como pensamos. P. La gente puede pensar que hay dos líderes como Juan y Enric. ¿Se van a entender? R. Seguro que sí. Es un Mundial muy duro, en el que al final van a hablar las piernas. Será cuestión de quién se encuentre mejor. Incluso tener esa superioridad numérica, con dos corredores delante, puede jugar a nuestro favor. Se van a entender. Los dos tienen la madurez y la cabeza necesarias para saber que tener dos corredores ahí puede jugar a favor. Yo creo que sabremos aprovecharlo. P. A nivel personal, en un principio no iba a estar en el Mundial. ¿Cómo lo ha vivido? R. Para mí estar aquí me hacía bastante ilusión. Es un Mundial duro, no quedan tantos por delante y poder estar aquí me apetecía mucho. Además, viniendo Juan y Enric, con los que también he trabajado mucho tiempo, me hacía especial ilusión estar. La verdad es que bastante bien. Después del Tour corrí la Vuelta a Alemania, he entrenado bastante bien y he competido menos de lo que me hubiera gustado. Venir a LaVuelta desde casa fue un poco raro, pero también me ha dado ese puntito de frescura que para un Mundial es muy importante. Y venir aquí con un poquito de anterioridad para entrenar con Juan también ha sido bueno para estar adaptado y aclimatado. Ayer tuve una pequeña caída entrenando, que no fue nada. Espero que se quede en un susto. Ahora tengo ganas de quitar la carbonilla mañana y estar al cien por cien el domingo. P. ¿Y los resultados ya se están viendo? R. Se están viendo. Llevamos unas cuantas medallas, de momento tres títulos mundiales si no me equivoco, y ahora esperamos el turno de las chicas mañana y el nuestro el domingo. A ver si podemos poner el colofón final a estos Mundiales, que de momento están siendo bastante provechosos. P. ¿Qué les ha dicho Alejandro Valverde? R. Todavía no hemos hablado. Mañana tenemos reunión antes de la carrera y plantearemos un poco la táctica. Yo creo que las cosas están claras: tanto Enric como Juan están en primera línea. Después tenemos un equipo bastante fuerte y compensado. Hay un mix de veteranía y juventud, y podemos hacer las cosas bien. P. A propósito de la temporada, hemos visto que Juan ha tenido subidas y bajadas. Empezó bien, luego tuvo problemas... ¿Cómo lo ve? R. Bien. En general creo que ha sido un buen año. Ha demostrado que es uno de los mejores corredores del mundo. Seguramente no ha sido un año de buena suerte. La caída de París-Niza lo cambió un poco todo y a partir de ahí ir un poco a contrapié no ha sido un camino fácil hasta el Tour. En el Tour lo pagó un poco, pero creo que es un año importante para el aprendizaje y para seguir creciendo como corredor. Todavía nos queda el domingo y Lombardía por delante para poner un buen broche a la temporada y acabar con el mejor sabor de boca posible. P. El ciclismo español está remontando. En este Mundial, con LaVuelta de Enric, las medallas aquí... parecía algo imposible hace no tanto. R. Sí. En la vida en general y en el ciclismo en particular todo son ciclos. Es una rueda. A veces toca estar arriba y otras abajo, pero tarde o temprano todo va a su sitio. Hemos tenido rachas regulares y ahora parece que estamos entrando en una mejor. A ver si continúa, como mínimo, hasta el domingo en el Mundial. P. Como veterano en el ciclismo español, ¿cómo lo vive? R. Bien. Creo que demuestra que el ciclismo es un deporte en el que la edad cuenta, claro, pero tampoco tanto. Incluso a veces cuenta a favor. Ahí está el propio Ion Izagirre, que está en su última temporada y ganando hasta el final. Creo que es una cuestión mental, de motivación, de estar enfocado, de tener claro lo que quieres hacer y de que te guste lo que haces. Si eso es así, no hay una edad concreta. Es más cuestión del momento y de disfrutarlo. Y cuando lo haces, como hemos visto con Landa, con Enric o con Jon, al final es cuestión de tiempo. P. Hablando un poco también del equipo, están llegando gallos, varios fichajes importantes. ¿No caben todos? R. Cambios, como ha dicho. Hay muchas especulaciones y no sabemos al cien por cien qué pasa con esos fichajes. Sabemos que hay nuevos corredores y que ha habido un proceso de cambio general en el equipo, empezando por el management. El año que viene seremos cien por cien alemanes, cambiando incluso el service course a Alemania. Hay cambios y creo que es bueno. Tenemos un equipo que está creciendo y estoy contento de formar parte del proceso. P. A nivel contractual, ahora que cambian las cosas en Lidl-Trek, ¿se cierra el contrato que tenía y se hace uno nuevo? ¿Se prolonga? ¿Cómo es? R. Buena pregunta. Tenemos un meeting en una semana y ahí nos darán más datos. Lo que está claro es que los contratos que están firmados son válidos y eso normalmente se tiene que respetar. P. Mirando hacia el final de temporada, hablaba de Lombardía. También para Juan, que será su primer monumento. Parece mentira que sea su primer monumento. ¿Cómo lo afronta? R. Yo, lo primero, pienso en el Mundial, que es el domingo. Y después en el final de temporada.

articles.title: Tim Tebow says he's pausing relationship with Christian organization after 'scam' allegations
articles.summary: Tebow was reportedly paid up to $100,000 per event as a speaker.
articles.body:
Tim Tebow is pausing his relationship with Life Surge in the wake of "scam" allegations against the Christian-focused organization he has helped front for years, he told reporters Friday.

The allegations were aired out an episode of the "Pablo Torre Finds Out" podcast published Thursday . Torre and co-investigator Kiera Butler of Mother Jones allege that Tebow has hosted dozens of events as part of a predatory business model that encourages attendees to eventually pay five-figure sums for financial education.

"The allegations are extremely, extremely serious and it's something that we take very serious. And so for us, we're having our team do an investigation but also pausing our relationship until we can learn more about the facts to be able to understand more."

Life Surge's website says its mission is to "Inspire, train, & equip others to SURGE their resources and influence for Kingdom Impact," while offering "1-day inspirational events," "3-day transformational classes" and "ongoing advanced training and mentorship."

According to the episode titled "We Investigated the Christian 'Scam' Fronted by Tim Tebow," Tebow has been paid between $50,000 and $100,000 to headline introductory events, in which attendees are charged only $30 to hear Tebow and others speak. A cascading series of subsequent classes are then offered, with five-figure prices to learn about topics like the stock market and real estate.

Throughout the day, members of the audience are offered opportunities to enroll in three days of "impact classes" for $97. Those who attend then have the chance to enroll in "SurgeU" — a series of courses promising to "surge your resources and influence through real estate and trade — for Kingdom impact." SurgeU doesn't come cheap: Packages range from about $10,000 to $40,000. Should you want to enroll but lack the cash, Life Surge connects you with a third-party lender.

Tebow, whose Christianity was central to his public persona during his football career, is recorded as having urged attendees to sign up for such classes at a 2023 Life Surge event:

"So I know that many of you today have probably signed up for classes, have probably signed up to take the next step," he said. "I want to encourage you to finish that, to follow through on that commitment, to finish strong."

The central pitch appears to be offering people financial training to help them make money and in turn advance their religious mission, even if it requires taking out lines of credit or pulling from retirement accounts.

One couple told Mother Jones they borrowed roughly $40,000 on interest-free credit cards after speaking with one of Life Surge's in-house financial counselors, only to make nothing from the stock market and have to take out a home equity loan to pay off the remaining debt, where the variable interest rate had increased to 29%.

Tebow didn't respond to Torre or Butler's requests for comment. On Friday, he said he only found out about the allegations on Thursday:

"I was at an anti-human trafficking conference yesterday and the team shared with me when we were leaving, as we were flying for Alabama for an event. Kind of caught off guard with some of it and I think that's why we're really trying to understand more of the facts to really learn it."

Tebow is far from the only athlete to have spoken for Life Surge, though he appears to be their most prolific paid speaker. Butler says he was on pace to do 23 different events across 2026.

Since the start of 2025 alone, Torre and Butler present bills featuring the likes of Joe Montana, Magic Johnson, Derek Carr, Marcus Mariota, Saquon Barkley, Cooper DeJean, Brandon Graham, Michael Strahan, Nick Foles, David Ortiz, Russell Wilson, Dominique Dawes, Jerome Bettis and Darryl Strawberry. Former ESPN host Sage Steele is also alleged to have participated in 10 events in 2026 alone.

Life Surge's website also lists Emmitt Smith, Cris Carter, Mark Few, Jeremiah Smith, Calvin Johnson, Brian Dawkins, Joe Mazzulla, Bob Stoops, Brian Urlacher, Antonio Gates and David Robinson among its speakers.

Tebow hasn't played an NFL game since 2012, but he has remained in the public sphere in a number of ways, from a minor-league baseball career to stints on the ESPN family of networks to Congressional testimony about the spread of human trafficking.

articles.title: US coach Pochettino regrets his limited role in Balogun red-card appeal at the World Cup
articles.summary: U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino says he should have been more involved in the decision to appeal the red card given to star forward Folarin Balogun during the...
articles.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. (AP) — U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino says he should have been more involved in the decision to appeal the red card given to star forward Folarin Balogun during the World Cup .

Balogun's suspension for the red card was lifted after President Donald Trump spoke to FIFA leadership, allowing him to play against Belgium in the round of 16. Balogun was the top scorer for the Americans with three goals when he received the red card in a 2-0 win over Bosnia-Herzegovina in the round of 32.

"At the time, I didn't fully understand the criticism," Pochettino said Friday ahead of the U.S. match Saturday against Peru. "But now, with the benefit of time and looking back on it, the truth is that you have to learn from things, from mistakes. And I think sometimes the things that happen during a tournament have to stay there."

FIFA lifted the suspension , allowing Balogun to play in the round of 16, an extraordinary move that triggered praise from Trump and outrage from Belgium. It appeared to be the first time since 1962 that a red card during a World Cup didn't result in a suspension.

Pochettino said Friday that the entire energy changed after the suspension was lifted. Analyzing that game now is difficult considering "it was not the best environment to go to compete in a World Cup," he said.

Belgium beat the U.S. 4-1 to reach the quarterfinals, and Balogun had little impact in the loss.

Pochettino signed a four-year contract to remain as coach through the 2030 World Cup. The first roster of his second term as coach was announced last week. Balogun, who hasn't played for Monaco this season after a possible transfer to Everton fell through, is not on the current U.S. roster. Pochettino cited a leg injury.
